title.narrative: South Asia Subregional Economic Cooperation Power System Expansion Project

description.narrative: ADB assisted the Government of Nepal in increasing capacity of national power grid and enhancing renewable energy development. The South Asia Subregional Economic Cooperation Power System Expansion Project is building more than 200 kilometers of power transmission lines, as well as substations, along Kali Gandaki corridor in the Himalayas and Marsyangdi-Kathmandu route. The project is also building or upgrading more than 1,000 kilometers of power distribution lines in the east, central, and west regions of the country. To bring affordable renewable energy to remote areas, the project is building small hydroelectric power plants, as well as mini-grid based solar and solar/wind hybrid energy systems.

30,500 additional households supplied by renewable energy in rural communities by 2025 Achievement: 19863 Progress/Status: 19,863 households have been supplied with renewable energy. Data Source: NEA annual reports, and SASEC Energy Working Group meeting minutes

CO2 emissions reduced by 20,000 tons per year by 2025 Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: Not yet due. Will be assessed approaching completion of project implementation. Data Source: NEA annual reports, and SASEC Energy Working Group meeting minutes

Distribution capacities in identified areas increased to 316 MVA by 2025 (Baseline: 100 MVA in 2011) Achievement: 3 Progress/Status: Contracts for distribution system expansion in eastern and western Nepal are ongoing. Out of 25 substations, 20 are complete and the rest are under construction. Distribution system reinforcement and substation augmentation works are completed. Works for Dhalkebar- Mujeliya 33 kV line upgradation is completed. Data Source: NEA annual reports, and SASEC Energy Working Group meeting minutes

Power evacuation capacity from Kali Gandaki basin and Marsyangdi basin increased to 1,000 MW by 2025 (Baseline: 100 MW in2013) Achievement: 1941 Progress/Status: Dana-Kusma 220 kV transmission line and associated substations at Dana and Kusma, Kusma-New Butwal 220 kV transmission line, New Butwal-Bardaghat 220 kV transmiision line, New Butwal substation, Marsyangdi-Kathmandu 220 kV transmission line, Matatirtha substation is complete. Markichowk substation is substantially complete.
Works under grid substation reinforcement project has been completed for all substations- Dhalkebar, Lahan, Damauli, Baneshwore, Banepa, New Kawasoti, Butwal, Bharatpur, Butwal, and Gandak. Data Source: AEPC annual reports, NEA annual reports, and SASEC Energy Working Group meeting minutes
